<a id="edition-cases-naval-black-sea-shipping"></a>

## Supply cargo at Nikolaev and the sale of Corcovado

**Sources on this page:** p199 A1, p199 A2, p199 A3. [Concise case study](../naval/black_sea_shipping.md).

**Shared edition.** The following reading also discusses [p200 B1](200.md#source-p200-b1), [p200 B2](200.md#source-p200-b2).

<a id="edition-cases-naval-black-sea-shipping-supply-cargo-at-nikolaev-and-the-sale-of-corcovado"></a>



**Source edition and recovery: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

**Prior identification of the p199 A body: George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils
Kopal and Arno Wacker (2016), §6.5.**

Five source records recover two distinct messages intercepted on November 15,
1918. The first reports on steamers and goods at Nikolaev and asks what the
recipient intends to do as circumstances change. The second orders that a
ship sale to Turkey, or the transfer of ownership following a sale, should
be stopped unless the stated payment condition is met.

Both messages use the published `Nov13-15b` partial square. They are separate
traffic, not overlapping copies of one plaintext. Literal source crops and
headers are in the [source edition](../../experiments/black_sea_shipping/inputs.json),
and each geometric choice and coordinate repair is in the
[exact certificate](../../experiments/black_sea_shipping/certificates.json).
The primary source is J. Rives Childs, *General Solution of the ADFGVX Cipher
System*, printed pp. 199–200, PDF pp. 202–203.

Lasry and colleagues already describe the p199 supply message in
[their paper](https://doi.org/10.1080/01611194.2016.1169461), §6.5, *A Code
within a Code* (author PDF p. 25, printed p. 24). The work added here for p199
is the exact source edition, the full set of frame alternatives and
coordinate-level repair certificates. Its body identification is credited
to that prior publication. Their approximate ten-ton paraphrase differs from
the `120`-ton field obtained below under the conditional shared digit reading.

<a id="edition-cases-naval-black-sea-shipping-the-three-part-supply-message-p199-a"></a>

### The three-part supply message, p199 A

The common source header reads `XYZ v LP (06.01 p.m., November 15th)`,
`16.50 (15/11)`, `3 TLE`. It belongs to the correspondence using
`FEIGENHAUS`, `HERKULES` and `REICHSVERSORGUNG`, also seen in the earlier
[p120/p123 messages](../naval/p120_p123.md). The new reference is written out as
`SECHSHUNDERTACHTZEHN` (618); the earlier message has 617. This is further
correspondence, not a retransmission of the previously published text.

<a id="edition-cases-naval-black-sea-shipping-a1-incoming-steamers-and-a-garbled-cargo-description"></a>

#### A1: incoming steamers and a garbled cargo description

**Readable German — existing source frame and word repairs, with conditional VG=2:**

> An Feigenhaus sechshundertachtzehn. Herkules meldet zwoelften November, dass Nikolajew mehrere Dampfer LEBER Kakaopulver aus OPERETTE, zirka 120 Tonnen, eingelaufen.

The [shared award-class interpretation](../../experiments/nov13_joint_completion/README.md#the-award-class)
assigns **VG=2**, completing the quantity `1?0` as **120** and fixing
**146/146** labels in this edition. The quantity's pair is formed by observed
source coordinates **52 and 235**; no new repair is required.

The source advertises `RICHI-292`, but prints **293 valid coordinates**.
Its tenth group is the six-letter `XAXADV`. Removing its final `V`, source
index 50, gives this 146-position raw decryption:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — conditional removal of the final V in six-coordinate group XAXADV:**

```text
ANFEIGENHAUSSECHSHUNDERTACHTZEHNXHERKULESMELDETZWOEZFTENNOVEMBERDASSNIKOLAJEWMEHREREDAMPFERLEBERKAKAUPULSERAUSXOPERETTEXZIRKA1?0TONNENEINGELAUFENX
```

</details>

It addresses Feigenhaus and reports Herkules's news of November 12 about
several steamers entering Nikolaev. The cargo wording is damaged. Three
observed-coordinate substitutions support the same-length ordinary-word
repairs `ZWOELFTEN` and `KAKAOPULVER`:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output — same conditional single-coordinate deletion, followed by word repairs:**

```text
ANFEIGENHAUSSECHSHUNDERTACHTZEHNXHERKULESMELDETZWOELFTENNOVEMBERDASSNIKOLAJEWMEHREREDAMPFERLEBERKAKAOPULVERAUSXOPERETTEXZIRKA1?0TONNENEINGELAUFENX
```

</details>

`LEBER` remains unexplained, and `OPERETTE` remains an unidentified code word.
The displayed baseline streams retain `1?0`; the readable text above applies
the shared conditional digit assignment.

The deletion is not called globally unique. When names, the `LEBER` segment
and the quantity are masked, deleting source index 50, 51 or 52 gives the same
minimum of three ordinary-word coordinate changes. Only index 50 lies inside
the visibly six-letter source group. The certificate retains all three
broader models, including the alternatives' changed code-name/quantity text.
With VG=2, the source-50 and source-51 exclusions both yield `120`; the
source-52 exclusion still gives `1G0`. The new digit does not establish a
unique source geometry.

<a id="edition-cases-naval-black-sea-shipping-a2-goods-remain-aboard-under-military-guard"></a>

#### A2: goods remain aboard under military guard

All 344 source coordinates are valid. The raw 172-position reading is:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
DASCHWALBENSCHWANZUNDABTRANVPORTABNIKO?AJEWELSEVORLAEUFIGUNMOEGLICHXWAREBLEIBTDAHERUNTERMILITAERISCHERBEWACHUNGANBORDXVERSUCHETDURCHVORZUGSKARTENDARUEBERNAEHERESZUERFAHRENX
```

</details>

Two observed-coordinate changes restore `ABTRANSPORT` and `NIKOLAJEW`,
giving a complete, exactly reencryptable candidate:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
DASCHWALBENSCHWANZUNDABTRANSPORTABNIKOLAJEWELSEVORLAEUFIGUNMOEGLICHXWAREBLEIBTDAHERUNTERMILITAERISCHERBEWACHUNGANBORDXVERSUCHETDURCHVORZUGSKARTENDARUEBERNAEHERESZUERFAHRENX
```

The plain passage says that the goods therefore remain aboard under military
guard, and asks the recipient to obtain more information through

<a id="edition-cases-naval-black-sea-shipping-a3-uncertainty-about-the-recipients-plans"></a>

#### A3: uncertainty about the recipient's plans

There are 205 printed slots under `RICHI-206`. The malformed group is
`VAYA`, and the next group has an overstruck first glyph recorded as `?`.
The certificate tests all 206 possible single-coordinate insertion boundaries
with the whole footer excluded from the stencil.

Five positions, **164–168**, tie at **zero changes to observed coordinates**
for the ordinary-word body. Gap 165 is a representative, not an established
unique location. Its raw reading is:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — conditional missing-slot placement at gap 165; equivalent alternatives retained:**

```text
SINDBEUNR?HIGTDANICHTWISS?NWASIHRINANBETRACHTLAGEBEGINNENWERDETXREICHSVERSORGUNGXADMIRALSTAB15?16DZWCIX
```

</details>

Filling two source erasures gives:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output — same conditional gap model, with the two stated fills:**

```text
SINDBEUNRUHIGTDANICHTWISSENWASIHRINANBETRACHTLAGEBEGINNENWERDETXREICHSVERSORGUNGXADMIRALSTAB15?16DZWCIX
```

</details>

The sender is concerned because it does not know what the recipient will do
in view of the situation. The message ends with `REICHSVERSORGUNG` and
`ADMIRALSTAB`. All five tied models can be filled to this same **92-character
prefix**, without changing an observed coordinate. Their footer readings
differ and are all retained in the certificate.

A separate footer proposal reads `15X16DZWEIX`, filling the separator and
changing one observed coordinate to turn `ZWCI` into `ZWEI`. It is explicitly
editorial; the footer does not select the ordinary-body gap model and does
not establish a new digit assignment.

<a id="edition-cases-naval-black-sea-shipping-the-two-part-ship-sale-order-p200-b"></a>

### The two-part ship-sale order, p200 B

The common source header is `NKJ v LP (08.19 p.m., November 15th)`,
`16.00 (15/11) FUER COS`, `2 TLE`. The received ship name is `CORCOWADO`.
The association with Corcovado is kept separate from that literal spelling.

<a id="edition-cases-naval-black-sea-shipping-b1-stop-the-sale-or-ownership-transfer"></a>

#### B1: stop the sale or ownership transfer

The first part has 394 source slots. The last glyph in group 7, `AAXFY`,
is an invalid coordinate `Y` and remains an erasure in the raw reading:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
MXMXDXNICOLAJEFFXWENNVERKAUFXCORCOWADOXANTUERKEINOCINICHTINORDNUNGSOLLVERKAUFNI?HTSTA?TFINDENXFALLSAUFGRUNDBEREITSGETAETIGTENVERKAUFSEIGENTUMSUEBERTRAGUNGNOCHWICHTERFOLGTISTHATSOLCHEZUUNTERBLEIBENX
```

</details>

Three observed-coordinate substitutions and one invalid-glyph fill give
this complete 197-position candidate:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
MXMXDXNICOLAJEFFXWENNVERKAUFXCORCOWADOXANTUERKEINOCHNICHTINORDNUNGSOLLVERKAUFNICHTSTATTFINDENXFALLSAUFGRUNDBEREITSGETAETIGTENVERKAUFSEIGENTUMSUEBERTRAGUNGNOCHNICHTERFOLGTISTHATSOLCHEZUUNTERBLEIBENX
```

</details>

Addressed to `M. M. D., Nicolajeff`, it says that if the sale to Turkey has
not yet been settled, it should not take place. If a sale has already been
made but ownership has not yet been transferred, that transfer must not
proceed. This is the message's historical instruction, not an inference
about what ultimately happened to the ship.

<a id="edition-cases-naval-black-sea-shipping-b2-payment-in-germany-before-ownership-transfer"></a>

#### B2: payment in Germany before ownership transfer

All 360 printed slots are retained. One glyph is unreadable and another is
an `E`-like overstrike, both preserved as source erasures. The raw text is:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
TUERKEIGEGENUEBERKNNGELTENDGEMCHTWERDENXREED?REIWILLDAMPFERANTUEKEINICHTVERKAUFENESSEIDENNDASSKAUFPREISINDEUTSCHLANDVOREIGENTUMSUEBERTRAGUNGBARBEZAHLTWERDEXMARIN?AMTXAXSECHSXS????0
```

</details>

Filling those two erased coordinates recovers `REEDEREI` and `MARINEAMT`,
without changing any observed valid coordinate:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
TUERKEIGEGENUEBERKNNGELTENDGEMCHTWERDENXREEDEREIWILLDAMPFERANTUEKEINICHTVERKAUFENESSEIDENNDASSKAUFPREISINDEUTSCHLANDVOREIGENTUMSUEBERTRAGUNGBARBEZAHLTWERDEXMARINEAMTXAXSECHSXS????0
```

</details>

The message supplies the position to present to Turkey: the shipowner will
not sell the steamer unless the purchase price is paid in cash in Germany
before ownership transfers. The source omits letters in `KNN`, `GEMCHT` and
`TUEKEI`; those strings are not silently length-corrected in the candidate.
The footer's four baseline unknowns use cells `VG`, `VG`, `GD`, `AD`.
The shared conditional VG=2 reading gives **`S22??0`**, taking this edition
from **176 to 178/180** fixed labels. The two remaining cells are unassigned;
the two earlier erasure fills and the source's omitted letters are unchanged.

<a id="edition-cases-naval-black-sea-shipping-exact-scope-and-reproducibility"></a>

### Exact scope and reproducibility

The five records have 1,596 printed slots, 1,591 valid coordinates and 798
modeled plaintext positions. The declared source models fix 785 positions
before repairs. Conservative candidates fix 792; the shared conditional
VG=2 reading adds **three** labels, reaching **795/798**. Fixed counts include
received garbles and therefore do not mean that every word is restored.

The [shared-traffic certificate](../../experiments/nov13_joint_completion/traffic_certificates.json)
checks these three digits against the original coordinates and retains all
three equally priced A1 exclusion models.

The [verifier](../../experiments/black_sea_shipping/verify.py) recomputes every
plaintext domain and source mapping, the broad and source-local deletion
results, all five gap ties, and each exact repair. It checks the separate
conditional `FX=Y` hypothesis against 21 variants, retaining all effects:
there are no newly fixed raw letters, only listed domain reductions. No
published key file is changed.

<a id="edition-cases-caucasus-tiflis-appointment"></a>

## A Polish representative in Tiflis — p199 preamble and p192 parts 2 and 3

**Sources on this page:** p199 unlettered part 1. [Concise case study](../caucasus/tiflis_appointment.md).

**Shared edition.** The following reading also discusses [p192 part 2](192.md#source-p192-2), [p192 part 3](192.md#source-p192-3).

<a id="edition-cases-caucasus-tiflis-appointment-a-polish-representative-in-tiflis--p199-preamble-and-p192-parts-2-and-3"></a>


[Case index](../README.md) · [November 14 retransmissions](../radio/nov14_radio_retransmissions.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source edition, missing-group recovery and historical comparison: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

The two unheaded parts at the top of printed page 192 describe an appointment
to represent the Polish government in the Caucasus. The first is directly
readable under the published November 13–15b key. The second becomes readable
after an explicitly certified missing five-coordinate group. Its courier
surname provides independent historical support for the conditional key
assignment **FX = Y**.

A later source check recovered a matching preamble on printed p199. It asks
General von Kress in Tiflis to forward the Polish Foreign Ministry's message
to **Waclaw v. Ostrowski**. The text supplies the recipient directly. Its
association with the unheaded p192 parts is strong, but their conflicting
page/header dates are not silently reconciled.

<a id="edition-cases-caucasus-tiflis-appointment-readable-meaning"></a>

### Readable meaning

**Readable German — the base edited text, with the courier name still unresolved:**

> An General von Kress, Tiflis. Nr. `?1?`. Bitte Weiterleitung folgenden Telegramms des Ministerium des Aeusseren in Warschau an Herrn Waclaw v. Ostrowski, Tiflis: Sie sind zum Vertrauensmann der polnischen Regierung fuer die Republiken Grusien, Armenien und Aserbejnzan mit Sitz in Tiflis ernannt. Ernennung und Instruktion bereits durch `T?DE?SKI` an Sie abgesandt. Ministerium des Aeussern. Bussche.

**Display notes:** This combines the separately identified parts under the cross-page association discussed below. It supplies word spacing, capitalization and punctuation; the colon renders the transmitted word `DOPPELPUNKT`. The spellings `ASERBEJNZAN`, `AEUSSERN` and the missing genitive S in `DESMINISTERIUM` remain unnormalized in the base text. The reference and both name positions remain unknown.

**English meaning with a conditional historical-name interpretation:**

> To General von Kress, Tiflis: Please forward the following telegram from
> the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Warsaw to Mr. Waclaw v. Ostrowski,
> Tiflis: You have been appointed the Polish government's trusted
> representative for the republics of Georgia, Armenia and Azerbaijan,
> with your seat in Tiflis. The appointment and instructions have already
> been sent to you through [Tydelski]. Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Bussche.

The bracketed surname `[Tydelski]` is a historical identification, not an abbreviation expansion or a direct rendering of the unresolved base name. It uses the historical identification described below.
The opening uses the newly sourced p199 preamble and its explicit cross-page
association. Its source header is dated November 15, 1918, while p192 is
headed November 14. Neither is established as the appointment telegram's
original issue date; a forwarding date need not be an issue date.

<a id="edition-cases-caucasus-tiflis-appointment-part-1-on-p199-the-recipient-and-a-floating-group"></a>

#### Part 1 on p199: the recipient and a floating group

The unlettered message following p199 A is headed `NKJ v LP (08.32 p.m.,
November 15th)`, `FUER COS 18.56 (15/11)`, `3 TLE`, and `1 TL RICHI-262`.
It has 257 valid coordinates in the main grid and a separate printed `FGFFF`
above it. All 262 valid coordinates are preserved. The main grid also has a blank cell
at row 6, column 5; the blank is not silently supplied with five erasures.

Reading the floating group first, in physical top-to-bottom order, gives:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — floating group read first in physical top-to-bottom order:**

```text
ANGENERALVO?KRESSTI5LISXNRXZ1?XBITTEWEITERLEITUNGFODGENDENTILEGRAMM6DESMTNISTERIUMDESAEUSSELSNINWARSCHAUANHERRNXWACLAWXVXOSTROWSKIX
```

</details>

The source's unusual layout is resolved independently of the personal names.
The certificate places the five observed floating coordinates at all **258**
boundaries of the main grid and compares a declared ordinary-word stencil.
It masks `KRESS`, `TIFLIS`, `WARSCHAU`, the entire `WACLAW V OSTROWSKI` field,
and the reference. The unique minimum places `FGFFF` after the first **10**
main-grid coordinates, as the third group. It needs only two changes to
ordinary-word coordinates; the literal top-first placement needs seven under
the same masked stencil. This movement adds and removes no coordinate.

The selected geometry gives 129 fixed raw positions out of 131:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — conditional placement of the floating group after ten main-grid coordinates:**

```text
ANGENERALVONKRESSTIFLISXNRX?1?XBITTEWEITERLEITUNGFOLGENDENTELEGRAMMSDESMTNISTERIUMDESAEUSSERSNINWARSCHAUANHERRNXWACLAWXVXOSTROWSKIX
```

</details>

Two observed-coordinate substitutions restore `MINISTERIUM` and
`AEUSSEREN`:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output — same conditional floating-group placement, followed by the stated repairs:**

```text
ANGENERALVONKRESSTIFLISXNRX?1?XBITTEWEITERLEITUNGFOLGENDENTELEGRAMMSDESMINISTERIUMDESAEUSSERENINWARSCHAUANHERRNXWACLAWXVXOSTROWSKIX
```

</details>

The received `MINISTERIUM` lacks the genitive `S` expected in this formula.
The [shared conditional VG=2 reading](../../experiments/nov13_joint_completion/README.md#the-award-class)
completes the first reference digit: **`21?`**, giving **130/131** labels in
the preamble. This uses the existing floating-group placement and its two
word repairs, with no new source edit. The baseline quotation and streams
above retain `?1?` for comparison.

The association with p192 is supported by complementary part numbers,
the same published key, and continuous address/appointment syntax: p199 ends
with Ostrowski, while p192 part 2 begins `TIFLISDOPPELPUNKT` followed by the
appointment. It remains a cross-page association, not a surviving common
header. The November 14/15 discrepancy is real. The separate p192 A and B
records also combine November 14 receipt dates with `15/11` originating
dates, so the anomaly is documented elsewhere on that page as well. Mądzik's
study of Ostrowski in Tbilisi is corroborating context after this source
reading, and supplies no name crib to the group-placement test.

<a id="edition-cases-caucasus-tiflis-appointment-the-separate-historical-name-inference"></a>

### The separate historical-name inference

Marek Mądzik's [archival study](https://bazhum.muzhp.pl/media/texts/rocznik-lubelski/1987-1988-tom-29-30/rocznik_lubelski-r1987_1988-t29_30-s77-87.pdf#page=3),
printed p78 note 3, names engineer Tadeusz Tydelski as chairman of the Polish
Caucasus council, citing CAW relacje 400.2500, appendix 2, p3. Pages 78–79
also connect him with Ostrowski's Baku office. The article and
[short name crop](../../experiments/tiflis_appointment/sources/madzik_p78_name.png)
were checked; the underlying manuscript was not. Identifying this courier
with that person remains a separate inference.

Under that identification, `T?DE?SKI` becomes `TYDELSKI`. It supplies the
missing L coordinate and sets **FX = Y** in the November 13–15b square.
The full candidate then reads:

**Conditional interpretation — historical TYDELSKI identification, missing-coordinate fill and FX = Y:**

```text
MITSITZINTIFLISERNANNTXXERNENNUNGUNDINSTRUKTIONBEREITSDURCHXTYDELSKIXANSIEABGESANDTXXMINISTERIUMDESAEUSSERNXXBUSSCHE
```

Its exact repair certificate has **one observed-coordinate substitution**
and **five inserted coordinates**, `GFGFA`, at the declared gap. Full
reencryption reproduces that repaired ciphertext exactly. The historical
key file remains unchanged.

This check alone does not prove Y: the same repaired ciphertext can encode
`T2DELSKI`, `T3DELSKI`, `T4DELSKI`, `T7DELSKI`, `T8DELSKI`, `T9DELSKI`,
`TQDELSKI` or `TYDELSKI` under the eight possible cell assignments. The
independent historical surname supplies the reason to select Y.

<a id="edition-cases-caucasus-tiflis-appointment-consequences-for-the-pilot-notices"></a>

### Consequences for the pilot notices

Two inference layers are kept distinct:

| Layer | Assignment | Additional assumption | Complete-pair effects in these editions |
|---|---|---|---|
| Historical courier name | Nov13–15b FX = Y | The damaged courier name identifies Tydelski with correct spelling | p192 part 3 position 61; p190 A position 37 becomes FRYE |
| Cross-key pilot-name transfer | Nov13–15a DG = Y | The p190 A and p194 B FR?E fields contain the same correctly copied name | p194 B position 54 and interrupted p193 B position 54 |

Positions are zero-based. The first assignment does not depend on the pilot's
identity. The second remains conditional even if the Tydelski identification
is accepted. The machine-readable report includes every before/after raw
text and marginal-domain change across the three Tiflis records and all seven
[November 14 records](../radio/nov14_radio_retransmissions.md), including changes that
do not create another fixed letter.

The three records contain 719 valid source coordinates. The declared
724-coordinate frame fixes 354/362 raw positions before repairs, 358/362
after the ordinary-word layer, and 360/362 under the historical-name layer.
The p192 subset is unchanged at 225/231, 229/231 and 231/231. The further
VG=2 interpretation leaves one unresolved reference symbol in the p199
preamble and is compatible with the separate historical-name layer.
Raw fixed positions include source garbles; these counts describe the
mathematical consequences of each explicitly stated layer.
